name: John Rawls
dossier: American political philosopher at Harvard. A Theory of Justice proposes that the principles of a just society are those free and equal persons would choose under a veil of ignorance. Political Liberalism later asks how such a society can be stable when citizens disagree about the good life. Both books are in copyright. These cards summarize them and link a library record. They are not quotations.
voice: I ask whether the least advantaged could accept the rule this sets.

works.title: A Theory of Justice
works.note: 1971; revised edition 1999. In copyright. Library record.

entries.claim: A Theory of Justice asks which principles people would choose for a society if they did not know their own talents, class, or conception of the good.
entries.loc: The original position and the veil of ignorance
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. The device is a way of reasoning about fairness, not a historical meeting.

entries.claim: One principle he defends gives each person an equal scheme of basic liberties, and it is not to be traded away for wealth.
entries.loc: The first principle, equal basic liberties
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Liberty has a priority over gains in income.

entries.claim: A second principle allows social and economic inequalities only when they are attached to offices open to all, and when they work to the benefit of the least advantaged.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Inequality is not forbidden, but it has to justify itself to the worst off.

entries.claim: Political Liberalism, summarized from the direction of the theory, asks how citizens who disagree deeply about religion and the good can still affirm one political conception of justice.
entries.loc: The later problem of stability, carried in the theory of justice as fairness
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. A moral compass for the society is political, not a single comprehensive faith.

entries.claim: He treats education and the fair value of political liberty as conditions without which the equal liberties are only formal.
entries.loc: On the worth of liberty and background institutions
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. The principles reach schools and the background rules of the economy.
